The `at_start` guard only covers `cand.start() == 0`, not mid-haystack line starts (the common case).

The fix: when the candidate starts at a line start, first try the "no prefix strip" interpretation (since `^` is preferred in the alternation and matches empty there), verify it with the anchored original regex, and only fall back to the strip interpretation. The suffix side is safe because `$` can only participate at the haystack end (before a `\n`, `\W` is preferred and matches the `\n`), which is already guarded by `at_end -> Err`.

The fix is complete and validated. Summary:

## Root cause
`--word-regexp` is implemented by rewriting the pattern as `(?m:^|\W)(pat)(?m:$|\W)` (crates/regex/src/config.rs:305), where the true match is capture group 1. The `WordMatcher::fast_find` optimization (crates/regex/src/word.rs) found the overall match and then *assumed* it was sandwiched between `\W` characters, stripping one character from each end. But the leading alternation prefers `^` — a **line** anchor that matches at the start of *any* line, not just the haystack start (the old `at_start` guard only covered `cand.start() == 0`). At a mid-haystack line start, `^` participates and the first character of the overall match belongs to the real match, yet the fast path stripped it anyway — e.g. matching `ome.domain.com` instead of `some.domain.com` on line 2 of the issue's file.

## Fix (crates/regex/src/word.rs)
- When the overall match begins right after a `\n` (i.e., `^` may have participated), first try the **unstripped** interpretation: since `^` is the preferred branch, if the anchored original regex matches the unstripped span, that is provably the correct inner match.
- Otherwise fall back to the existing strip-one-leading-char interpretation (valid because the `\W` branch necessarily participated).
- The suffix side needs no new logic: `$` can only participate at the haystack end (before a `\n`, `\W` is preferred and matches the `\n` itself), which is already guarded by the `at_end → Err` bail-out.
- Extracted the shared inner-match confirmation checks (`inner_impossible`, line-terminator blocking, `strip_from_match`, anchored `original.is_match`) into `confirm_inner`, used by both interpretations.
- Added a regression test `regression_multi_line_start` mirroring the issue.

- A differential harness compared `find_at` (fast path) against `captures_at` (always-correct slow path) across 14 patterns × 11 multi-line haystacks × every byte offset — zero mismatches, including multi-byte and `(?-u)` byte-mode patterns.
- End-to-end: `rg -w -o '([\w]+[.])*domain[.](\w)+'` now prints three full `some.domain.com` matches; `-w -r`, `-w -o '\w+'` and other word-flag cases behave correctly.
